episodes.197341: A stalled trough of low pressure brought windy conditions and heavy rains to Kodiak Island which caused high water and lowland flooding across the area.
episodes.198720: On December 9, 2024, a slow-moving cold front interacting with a deep moisture plume resulted in prolonged periods of heavy rainfall across southeastern Louisiana. Widespread rainfall totals of 4 to 8 inches were reported, with localized amounts exceeding 10 inches, particularly in the river parishes portions of the Northshore. The excessive rainfall led to flash flooding, with numerous road closures.

events.narrative: Kodiak Airport reported 4.27 inches of rain which drove area rivers up, and flooded low lying roads, ditches and areas with poor drainage.  The Terror River crested at 5.26 ft at 10:30PM AKST; this is 0.26 ft above minor flood stage.
Ideal Street near Highway 70 was barricaded due to high water. Water was approaching some homes.
NWS employee sent a picture of flooding at the intersection of Albert and Florida in Mandeville.
NWS employed reported flooding on the Highway 190 service road near Judge Tanner.
A CO-OP observer reported that Lee Street in Donaldsonville was completely covered with water and impassible.
